name: No-Boil Chicken Pasta Casserole with Artichokes and Peas

prose.intro_html:
Here is the thing about a casserole that never asks you to boil the pasta: it respects your time and your grocery budget in the same breath. This No-Boil Chicken Pasta Casserole with Artichokes and Peas takes raw penne, cubed chicken breast, and a blender sauce built on cottage cheese and Boursin, then lets the oven do the work while you go do something else.

The numbers are why I keep coming back to it. Every one of the 14 servings lands at 603 calories with a serious 54.8 grams of protein. That is a dinner that eats like comfort food and reads like a training plan. The artichokes and lemon keep it bright, the parmesan browns on top, and nobody at the table has to know how little work it took.
prose.shop_smart:
This one leans on pantry and dairy-case staples, so shop the sizes, not the singles.

  • You need 1 lb 12 oz of dry penne. Most boxes run 16 oz, so plan on two boxes and pocket the leftover for the next round.
  • Cottage cheese and Boursin are the entire sauce. Pick up a full 2 lb 5 oz of cottage cheese and enough Boursin to reach 12 oz, which is a little over two of the 5.2 oz packages. The blender does not care if the Boursin goes in crumbled.
  • Frozen peas earn their spot here on shelf life alone, and 2 1/3 cups is a light scoop out of a standard bag.
  • Canned artichoke hearts drained down to 1 lb 4 oz works out to about two and a third cans. Buy three cans so you are covered.
  • Two lemons handle both the 4 2/3 tbsp of juice and the zest, so zest them before you squeeze.
prose.make_it:
Heat the oven to 400 degrees F and lightly grease a 9x13 casserole dish. Building this out to the full 14 servings, you will want a second dish or a larger roasting pan, because this is more casserole than one 9x13 will hold.

Build the sauce in a blender or food processor. Combine the cottage cheese, Boursin, minced garlic, fresh lemon juice, lemon zest, and sea salt, then run it until smooth. Add the chicken broth and blend again until it is fully incorporated. It will look very thin, and that is exactly right. The pasta drinks it up in the oven.

Now dump and assemble. Lay the dry penne across the bottom, then scatter the cubed chicken breast, peas, and chopped artichoke hearts over the top. Pour the blended sauce over everything and press down until the pasta is completely submerged. Submerged is not optional, since any dry pasta sitting above the liquid line stays dry.

Cover the dish tightly with foil and bake for 40 minutes. Pull it out, take off the foil, and give it a good stir. The pasta should still be slightly undercooked at this point. Top with the parmesan and return it to the oven for another 5 to 10 minutes, bumping the temperature up if you want the top nice and golden. If the pasta already tastes done, just add the parmesan and let it rest.

Rest the casserole at least 10 minutes before you touch it, then finish with chopped parsley or basil and serve.
prose.portion_html:
This recipe is built to hit 14 even servings, so weigh, do not eyeball. Set your empty container on the scale, zero it out, and note the total cooked weight of the casserole, subtract the dish, and divide by 14. That per-container gram number is your portion. Scoop to the number and you get 14 boxes that each read 603 calories and 54.8 grams of protein, instead of a few heavy ones and a few sad ones.

Give the pan a good stir before you portion, because the chicken, peas, and artichokes settle under the sauce. Mix it up so every container gets its fair share of protein and vegetables, not just sauce and pasta.
prose.cost_closing_html:
Here is where it earns its spot in the rotation. All 14 servings come out to ${{cost_ps}} each, and for that you get 603 calories and 54.8 grams of protein per box. Go try to buy a high-protein prepared meal for that and see how far you get.

Cottage cheese and canned artichokes are doing the heavy lifting on cost, both of them cheap ways to add body and flavor, while the chicken breast carries the protein without a premium cut. That is the whole trick: spend on what feeds you and skip what only decorates.
prose.upsell_html:
Fourteen dinners, one bake, no boiling, and a protein number that actually holds up. That is the kind of math that makes meal prep stick instead of fizzling out by Wednesday.

If you want more dinners built like this one, where every number is real and every dollar is accounted for, the whole Thrifty Crew library runs you a dollar a month. One casserole like this pays for the membership many times over.

head.description: A no-boil chicken pasta casserole with artichokes, peas, and a creamy cottage cheese and Boursin sauce. Makes 14 meal-prep servings at 603 calories and 54.8g protein each.
head.keywords: no boil chicken pasta casserole, dump and bake casserole, high protein meal prep, chicken artichoke casserole, cottage cheese pasta sauce, budget meal prep dinner
steps: Heat the oven to 400 degrees F and lightly grease a 9x13 casserole dish. For the full 14 servings, use a second dish or a larger roasting pan.

In a blender or food processor, blend the cottage cheese, Boursin, minced garlic, lemon juice, lemon zest, and sea salt until smooth, then add the chicken broth and blend until fully incorporated. The sauce will be very thin.

Lay the dry penne across the bottom of the dish, scatter the cubed chicken breast, peas, and chopped artichoke hearts over the top, then pour the blended sauce over everything and press until the pasta is completely submerged.
Cover tightly with foil and bake 40 minutes. Uncover, stir well while the pasta is still slightly undercooked, top with the parmesan, and bake another 5 to 10 minutes until golden.
Rest at least 10 minutes, then finish with chopped parsley or basil and serve.
